selection_rationale: Use the 1.42 solar-mass configuration reported in the phase-transition cooling study as the reduced-model stellar mass.
Use the literature-reported 10^9 K initial core temperature for the young-star cooling integration.
Use the angular frequency transformed from the same PSR J1640-4631 timing record that supplies the period derivative and braking index, preserving internal timing consistency.
Start below the selected 5.12e17 kg/m^3 transition threshold so spin-down compression can produce an observable threshold crossing in the reduced model.
Use the directly reported 9.7228e-13 s/s timing value from PSR J1640-4631.
Use the review-reported onset near twice nuclear saturation density, with the explicit baryon-density-to-mass-density transformation recorded in the evidence candidate.
The source gives latent-heat physics but no unique equivalent temperature increment; use 5e7 K as a declared five-percent proxy for sensitivity analysis, not a measured value.
Use phase-transition cooling as the approved baseline and explicitly override this switch only in the audited comparison scenarios.
Use the braking index measured in the same controlled PSR J1640-4631 timing excerpt as the initial spin quantities.
Use a 10^5 yr effective cooling timescale for the first reduced energy-balance model while leaving detailed neutrino and heat-capacity microphysics unresolved.
Use a linear 10^-3 core-to-surface temperature proxy so the 10^9 K core baseline maps to an order-10^6 K surface temperature.
Choose the positive coefficient so loss of rotational support from the measured initial spin can raise central density through the selected transition threshold before complete spin-down.
